approach: In `planning_round` (crates/athena-core/src/run/planning.rs:141-165), keep the base effort in a local before the `round > 1 || mechanical_passes > 0` branch calls `planner_revision_setting`. After the call, compare the resulting effort with the base. If it differs (the existing function returns the base string unchanged when the key is unset, weaker or equal, so a difference means a stronger effort), the timeout passed to `agent_spec` is `cfg.planner_timeout_s * PLANNER_ESCALATED_TIMEOUT_FACTOR`, a doc-commented `const u64 = 2`, using `saturating_mul`. Otherwise it stays `cfg.planner_timeout_s`. The comment cites job 20261114-041123-hvyh (round 2 at xhigh ran 606 s against 600 s). No config key, no `Models` change, no prompt change. Tests drive the real `go` flow with the fake driver script and read `spec.timeout` from the `AgentInvocation`. CHANGELOG gets a Fixed entry. Deliverable scope: I plan three files, per criterion 4. Two of the five expected deliverables (config.rs, decisions.md) stay untouched. D179's "planner_timeout_s unchanged" tradeoff line is then stale (see open question).

decisions.choice: Scale only when the effort returned by planner_revision_setting differs from the planner's own effort; a model-only change does not scale.
decisions.reason: The request ties the time to effort escalation. planner_revision_setting (config.rs:377-393) returns the current effort string unchanged when the key is unset, weaker or equal, so a string comparison reuses the existing rule and cannot drift from it.

rejected.option: Re-rank efforts in planning.rs with EFFORT_LEVELS
rejected.why: Duplicates the logic already in planner_revision_setting.

rejected.option: Scale every call with round > 1 || mechanical_passes > 0
rejected.why: Would lengthen the limit for unescalated revisions; the brief says those keep planner_timeout_s.

decisions.choice: A fixed 2x constant in planning.rs named PLANNER_ESCALATED_TIMEOUT_FACTOR, no new config key.
decisions.reason: Criterion 3 asks for a named constant, and criterion 4 and the out-of-scope list leave athena.toml and defaults.toml unchanged. 2x gives 1200 s from 600 s; the 2x value is an estimate, based on one 606 s observation.

rejected.why: Needs config.rs, athena.toml and defaults.toml changes, which are out of scope.
Treats the symptom, lengthens round 1 and unescalated calls, and edits governance config.

decisions.choice: Do not scale planner_usd or the critic timeout.
decisions.reason: The request and the out-of-scope list cover only the planner's time limit. Preflight reserves money only (reading.rs:130-132), so it is unaffected by the time change.

rejected.why: Not requested; it changes the budget reserve.

files.purpose: Add the doc-commented constant PLANNER_ESCALATED_TIMEOUT_FACTOR and scale the planner timeout only when the revision effort differs from the base effort; update the `plan_round` doc comment with a line on the time limit.
Record `spec.timeout` in `run_for_revision`; add the escalated and unscaled time-limit tests.
Add a Fixed bullet under Unreleased citing job 20261114-041123-hvyh.

steps: In tests.rs, extend the `run_for_revision` seam (tests.rs:1371-1434) to also record `spec.timeout` per call, for example in a new `timeouts: Vec<(Role, Duration)>` field on `RevisionRun`, and add a helper `planner_timeouts()`. Update every place that builds or destructures the `calls` tuple (for example tests.rs:1497) so the file compiles.

In planning.rs, add `const PLANNER_ESCALATED_TIMEOUT_FACTOR: u64 = 2;` with a doc comment saying why: job 20261114-041123-hvyh ran round 2 at xhigh for 606 s against the 600 s planner_timeout_s, so a call whose effort is raised gets a longer limit; the value is an estimate.

In `planning_round`, keep `base_effort = effort.clone()` before the revision branch (planning.rs:144-147). After the branch, set `planner_timeout_s = if effort != base_effort { cfg.planner_timeout_s.saturating_mul(PLANNER_ESCALATED_TIMEOUT_FACTOR) } else { cfg.planner_timeout_s }`. Pass it to `agent_spec` at planning.rs:162 in place of `cfg.planner_timeout_s`. Leave the critic call (planning.rs:366) alone. Add one line to the `plan_round` doc comment (planning.rs:21-23) on the time limit.

Add the criterion 1 test `a_stronger_revision_effort_scales_the_planner_time_limit`: keys sonnet and xhigh, reader model HAIKU (planner effort high), critic revise then accept. Assert planner timeouts are `[600 s, > 600 s]`, and that they equal `[600, 1200]` s.

Add the criterion 2 tests `planner_time_limit_is_unscaled_*`: no keys; weaker keys with a SONNET planner; an effort key equal to the planner's `"high"`. Also assert that in a `bad_plan()` then `good_plan()` run with escalating keys, the first call is 600 s and the mechanical revision call is scaled. Every unscaled call is exactly 600 s.

Add a CHANGELOG.md bullet under `## [Unreleased]` / `### Fixed`: root cause (planning_round passed `planner_timeout_s` to a call whose effort was raised to `planner_revision_effort`), job 20261114-041123-hvyh (round 2, xhigh, 606 s, 600 s deadline), the fix (2x limit only when the revision effort is stronger; round 1 and unescalated calls unchanged), that the 2x is an estimate, and the tests by name.
Run `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked`, and confirm `git diff --stat` shows only the three files.

risks.risk: 2x (1200 s) may still be too short, or longer than needed; it rests on one 606 s observation.
risks.mitigation: The constant is named and documented as an estimate. A later change can make it a config key; the single use site is easy to change.

risks.risk: Effort equality could misjudge escalation if planner_revision_setting returned a different but equal-rank string.
risks.mitigation: Compare the effort string returned by planner_revision_setting with the base string. The function returns the base string unchanged for an unset, weaker or equal key (config.rs:386-391), so equal strings mean no escalation.

risks.risk: The product could overflow for an absurd planner_timeout_s.
risks.mitigation: Use `saturating_mul` and keep the factor a `u64` constant.

risks.risk: Widening the recorded call tuple in run_for_revision breaks the existing tests that destructure it (tests.rs:1497).
risks.mitigation: Step 1 changes the tuple in one helper and updates its two users, `of` and the `calls` field uses; the compiler flags every use.

risks.risk: A longer deadline lets a stuck escalated planner run up to twice as long before it stops.
risks.mitigation: The limit applies only to the planner call, which is read-only and capped by planner_usd, so a longer deadline adds time and no change to what the planner can write.

dependents.dependent: crates/athena-agent/src/claude.rs:592-612 (deadline = clock + spec.timeout; stall_window(spec.timeout, ...) at 598) and claude.rs:386-392 (retry takes the timeout left)
dependents.reason: These read only the Duration on the spec and derive the deadline, stall window and retry time from it. A longer value on an escalated call only lengthens the limit for that call; the logic is unchanged and no planner-specific behavior is read.

dependents.name: planner call cost reserve
dependents.reason: The reserve is computed from dollar caps (planner_usd, critic_usd), not from timeouts. Timeouts are not read, so the reserve is unchanged.

dependents.reason: The selection code is not edited; the plan only reads its result. The existing assertions check model, effort, records and UI lines, not the timeout, so they still pass.

It builds the repo with `repo_with_revision_keys(3, Some(SONNET), Some("xhigh"))` (planner_timeout_s = 600 at tests.rs:1338, planner effort high), runs a plan (critic revise, then accept) and records the Planner calls' `spec.timeout`.
demonstrations.observes: Round 1's planner call has timeout 600 s; the round 2 call, at xhigh, has a timeout greater than 600 s (1200 s with the 2x constant).

The test double returns canned plan and critique JSON and holds no timeout logic.

demonstrations.method: New tests in run/tests.rs. (a) `repo_with_revision_keys(3, None, None)` with a critic revise: every Planner `spec.timeout` is exactly 600 s, including round 2. (b) The weaker-key case `repo_with_revision_keys(3, Some(HAIKU), Some("medium"))` with reader model SONNET (as in tests.rs:1516-1533): both calls are exactly 600 s. (c) The effort key equals the planner's ("high"): 600 s. (d) The escalating config of criterion 1, round 1 and the mechanical pass in round 1 when `bad_plan()` is first: the first call is 600 s and the later calls at xhigh are scaled.

demonstrations.fails_without: If scaling applied to all revisions or to round 1, assertions (a)-(c) and the round 1 check would see 1200 s instead of 600 s.
demonstrations.seam: Same as criterion 1: `Athena::go` with `run_for_revision` and the fake script recording `spec.timeout`. It exists today; Step 1 adds the timeout field.

The timeout passed to `agent_spec` is the scaled value only on the branch where the revision effort differs from the base effort.
